title: Spectrum Aeromed expands engineering team with two new engineers
summary: The company has announced the addition of William “Bill” Engelking and Carson Tveito to its engineering team.
body_markdown:
Paul Engelking. Spectrum Aeromed


Spectrum Aeromed has announced the addition of William “Bill” Engelking and Carson Tveito to its engineering team, strengthening the company’s technical capabilities as it continues to support a growing range of aircraft platforms and customer programs.


Engelking joins Spectrum Aeromed with more than 13 years of aircraft engineering experience, most recently serving as a Staff Powerplant Systems Engineer at Cirrus Aircraft.


His background includes aircraft systems integration, certification and compliance, flight testing, engineering analysis, and technical documentation.


At Spectrum Aeromed, he will support the design and development of air medical equipment, including 3D modeling, engineering drawings, structural analysis, and documentation supporting FAA certification.


Carson Tveito. Spectrum Aeromed Photo


Tveito’s transition to a full-time engineering position continues a path that began with Spectrum Aeromed in May 2024 as a production intern. He later transitioned into a manufacturing engineering internship, followed by a mechanical engineering internship, becoming the first Spectrum Aeromed engineering student to gain experience in all three internship roles.


Tveito will graduate from North Dakota State University in December 2026 with a degree in mechanical engineering and will join Spectrum Aeromed full-time as an engineer following graduation.


“Bill and Carson bring two different but equally valuable perspectives to our engineering team,” said Shannon Schell, president of Spectrum Aeromed. “Bill brings extensive aircraft certification and systems experience, while Carson has developed a strong understanding of our products and processes through his progression at Spectrum. We’re excited to have both contributing to our continued growth.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Spectrum Aeromed.*
